newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy wants Albanian army to help keep peace.
newsitem.headline: Italy wants Albanian army to help keep peace.

text.p: Italy said on Monday it wanted Albanian army units to assume a peacekeeping role after an Italian-led multinational security force completes its withdrawal from the Balkan country.
"Before the end of the year we must try to bring some regiments of the Albanian army back into service," Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said in a statement.
"The defence ministry is studying a plan to reconstruct at least a few mobile regiments that could act as an element of internal security," he said.
The 7,000-strong multinational security force was deployed in April after anarchy swept Albania, with anti-government rebels looting Albanian army depots across the country.
The force is due to withdraw by August 12.

Rome will host an international conference starting later this week to assess the situation in Albania following general elections held on June 29 and July 6 in which the ex-communist Socialist party triumphed.
